behavior_class_name: Backdoor Persistence Service Foothold Behavior Class
description: Creates persistence by registering a scheduled task via the Task Scheduler COM API that executes based on a Windows Event Log trigger. The task monitors Security Event ID 4688 (process creation) and executes a marker payload when a specific process (firefox.exe) is launched. The payload writes a controlled artifact confirming persistence execution.

persistence_installer.role: initializes COM via .NET interop, connects to the Task Scheduler service, defines an event-triggered task using an XML subscription filter, and registers the task under SYSTEM context

marker_payload.role: benign executable launched when the event trigger condition is satisfied, continuously logging execution to confirm persistence behavior

persistence_installer: XML event subscription string referencing Security EventID 4688

registry: scheduled task registration stored under Task Scheduler subsystem
task configured with event-based trigger condition
process: marker process runs continuously after trigger
file_system: log file contains timestamped execution entries
host: Security Event Log contains Event ID 4688 entries
Task Scheduler Operational log may record task execution
task visible in Task Scheduler GUI
Sysmon Event ID 1 may capture marker process execution
network: no HTTP or HTTPS traffic is required
no TCP command channel is opened

code_placement: COM interop task creation and XML event subscription logic are implemented in the installer executable. Continuous execution logging behavior is implemented in the marker payload executable.
execution_trigger: The installer executes manually. The persistence payload executes when a matching Security Event ID 4688 is generated for firefox.exe process creation.
execution_target: Task Scheduler event trigger subsystem and marker executable at C:\Users\Public\A06_3b_SampleApp.exe
semantic_meaning: Demonstrates advanced event-driven persistence using Task Scheduler COM API, where execution is conditionally triggered by specific system events, reducing noise and increasing stealth compared to logon or time-based persistence.

mitre_attack_mapping.note: Event-triggered scheduled task persistence using COM API and Windows Event Log subscription.

control_notes.payload_effect: writes a controlled log file confirming event-triggered scheduled task execution

existing task A06_3b_EventTriggerTask is removed if present

task is registered under SYSTEM context
Task Scheduler matches event subscription filter
log file contains repeated timestamped entries confirming execution
